Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 55, verse 1–13:

Meccan, and it contains one thousand six hundred and thirty-six letters, three hundred and fifty-one words, and seventy-eight verses.

Al-Ustadh Abu al-Husayn al-Jabbari informed us, saying: I was told on the authority of Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kisani narrated to us, saying: Hisham al-Barbari narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hamza al-Kisai narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to us from his father Ja'far, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Ali, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Everything has a bride, and the bride of the Qur'an is Surat al-Rahman, may His remembrance be exalted." [163] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 1/582, no. 2638.]]

And Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Abdi informed me in the year three hundred and eighty-four, saying: Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Harbi informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk ibn al-Fadl al-Kufi narrated to us, saying:

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Sulaym al-Mada'ini narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir narrated to us from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Rahman, Allah will have mercy on his weakness and he will fulfil the thanks for what Allah has bestowed upon him." [164] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/326.]]

Hisham ibn Urwa narrated from his father, who said: The first to recite the Qur'an aloud in Mecca after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. That was because the Companions of the Messenger of Allah gathered and said: "The Quraysh have never heard the Qur'an recited aloud. Who among us will make them hear it?"

Ibn Mas'ud said: "I will." They said: "We fear for you from them; we want a man who has a clan that will protect him." He said: "Leave me, for Allah will surely protect me." Then he stood at the maqam and said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious, who taught the Qur'an," raising his voice with it, while the Quraysh were in their assemblies. They paid attention and said: "What is the son of Umm Abd saying?" Then they rose toward him and began beating him while he kept reciting, until he reached what he reached of it. Then he returned to his Companions, and they had left marks on his face. They said: "This is what we feared for you."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Most Gracious, who taught the Qur'an. It was revealed when they said: "What is the Most Gracious?" It was also said: it is an answer to the people of Mecca when they said: "It is only a human being who teaches him" (Q. 16:103).

Created man. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: this means Adam, peace be upon him.

Taught him expression (al-bayan). Ibn Abbas said: the names of every thing. It was also said: He taught him all languages; Adam, peace be upon him, spoke seven hundred thousand languages, the best of which was Arabic. Others said: it refers to all people, because "man" (al-insan) is a generic noun. Then they differed about the meaning of al-bayan. It is narrated from Qatada that he said: He taught him the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful, and made clear to him good and evil, and what to do and what to leave, so that He might thereby argue against him.

Abu al-Aliya, Murra al-Hamdani and Ibn Zayd said: it means speech. Al-Hasan said: articulation and discernment. Muhammad ibn Ka'b: what one says and what is said to him. Al-Suddi: He taught every people the tongue with which they speak. Yaman: writing and script with the pen; its parallel is "He taught by the pen" (Q. 96:4). Ibn Kaysan said: "Created man" means Muhammad (ﷺ), "taught him expression" means the explanation of what was and what will be, because he explained about the first and the last and about the Day of Judgment.

The sun and the moon run by a reckoning (bi-husban). That is, by calculation and fixed stations that you do not transgress. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatada and Abu Malik.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan said: by them is meant the reckoning of times, lifespans and terms. Were it not for night, day, the sun and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything. What if the whole age were night, how would you calculate? Or what if it were all day, how would you calculate? Al-Dahhak said: they run by a number. Mujahid: like the turning of a millstone, revolving around the axis of the mill. Al-Suddi: by a term like the terms of people; when their term comes, they perish. Its parallel is "each runs to a named term" (Q. 13:2 / 35:13). Yaman: they run with the people of the world, its decree and its passing away.

The word husban may be a verbal noun of "hasibtu hisaban" and "husbanan," like "ghufran," "kufran," "rujhan" and "nuqsan," and it may be the plural of hisab, like "shuhban," "ruhban," "qudban" and "rukban."

The nominative of "the sun and the moon" is by supposing a verb whose sense is: "the sun and the moon run by a reckoning." It was also said: it is a subject whose predicate is what follows.

The structure of the verse: "The Most Gracious taught the Qur'an" and "[He] determined the sun and the moon." It was also said: it is connected to "expression," meaning: He taught him expression, [and] that the sun and the moon are by a reckoning.

It is said: the extent of the sun is six thousand four hundred farsakhs in the like of it, and the extent of the moon is a thousand farsakhs by a thousand farsakhs.

It is written on the face of the sun: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; He created the sun by His power and set it running by His command." And on its belly is written: "There is no god but Allah. His pleasure is speech, His anger is speech, His mercy is speech, His punishment is speech." On the face of the moon is written: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; Allah created the moon, and created the darknesses and the light." And on its belly is written: "There is no god but Allah. He created good and evil by His power, by which He tests whom He wills of His creation. Blessed is the one through whose hands Allah makes good flow, and woe to the one through whose hands Allah makes evil flow."

And the star and the tree prostrate (yasjudan). It was said: it is what has no stem among trees and spreads over the face of the earth. Al-Suddi said: it is the collective term for plants; it was called a star (najm) because it rises (tala') from the earth, and their prostration is the prostration of their shadows. Mujahid and Qatada said: it is the constellation, and its prostration is its rising.

And the heaven, He raised it and set the balance (al-mizan). Mujahid said: justice. Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: it is that by which weighing is done, so that fairness and redress are attained. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the Qur'an. The root of weighing (al-wazn) is measurement.

That you not transgress (alla tatghaw) in the balance, meaning: lest you incline and wrong and exceed the truth in the balance. Establish the weight with justice (bi-l-qist), that is, with equity. Abu al-Darda said: set up the tongue of the balance with justice. Ibn Uyayna said: the establishing is with the hand, and the justice is with the heart. And do not make the balance deficient (la tukhsiru), that is, do not diminish the balance, and do not cheat in measure and weight.

Qatada said on this verse: "Be just, son of Adam, as you wish to be dealt with justly; and give full measure as you wish to be given full measure, for justice is the wellbeing of people."

The common reading is tukhsiru with a dammed ta' and a kasra on the sin. Bilal ibn Abi Burda read it with a fatha on the ta' and a kasra on the sin; both are dialectal forms.

And the earth, He laid it down for the creatures (lil-anam): for the created beings. Al-Hasan said: for jinn and humans. Ibn Abbas and al-Sha'bi said: for every living soul.

In it are fruits (fakiha). That is, the varieties of fruit. Ibn Kaysan said: that is what delights them with the uncounted blessings, and every blessing is a delight.

And the palm trees with sheaths (akmam): the containers of dates. Its singular is kumm; everything that covers us is a kumm and a kumma, and from it comes "kumm al-qamis" (the sleeve of a shirt). It is also said that a cap is called kumma. The poet said:

"I said to them: measure out with the cap of one of you / your dirhams, for I too measure in this way."

Al-Dahhak said: "dhat al-akmam" means possessing sheaths. Al-Hasan: its akmam are its fibres. Qatada: its necks. Ibn Zayd: the spathe before it splits open.

And the grain with its husk (al-habb dhu al-asf). Mujahid said: it is the leaves of the crop. Ibn al-Sikkit said: the Arabs call the leaves of the crop: al-asf, al-asifa and al-jull (with a kasra on the jim). Alqama ibn Abda said:

"It waters channels whose sprouting leaves have bent over; their roots are drawn from water that has been dragged in."

Al-asf: the green leaves of the crop when its heads are cut and it dries. Its parallel is "like a field eaten down" (Q. 105:5).

And the fragrant plant (al-rayhan). Mujahid said: it is provision (al-rizq), and this is the narration of Ikrima from Ibn Abbas, who said: every rayhan in the Qur'an is provision.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: al-rayhan means provision in the dialect of Himyar. The poet said:

"Peace from God and His rayhan, / His mercy and abundant rain."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: al-rayhan is al-rai' (produce). Al-Dahhak said: it is food. He said: al-asf is the fig, and al-rayhan is its fruit. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: it is your rayhan, this that is smelled. Al-Walibi, from Ibn Abbas, said: it is the greenness of the crop. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is what stands upon a stalk.

The common reading "wa al-habbu dhu al-asfi wa al-rayhanu" is all in the nominative, in coordination with "fakiha." Ibn Amir read all of them in the accusative, in the sense of "He created this man and He created these things." The people of Kufa, except Asim, read "wa al-rayhani" in the genitive, in coordination with "al-asf."

So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny (fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban), O you two jinn and humankind.

Evidence for this is what

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muslim al-Hanbali narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Khaliq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ibrahim al-Tarjumani narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Ammar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to us Surat al-Rahman until he finished it. Then he said: "What is wrong with you that I see you silent? The jinn gave a better response than you. Whenever I recited this verse to them, 'So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' they said: 'None of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny.'" [165] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/325, no. 4146.]]

Were you not naked and I clothed you? Will you deny this? Did I not carry you when you were riding? Will you deny this? Were you not obscure and I honoured you? Will you deny this? Were you not a celibate and I brought you to pilgrimage? Will you deny this?"

Repetition is permissible in Arab speech and is good in such a place. The poet said:

"..."

Another said:

"How many blessings were yours, how many, how many, and how many."

Another said:

"Fazara's party almost roasted us, so Fazara's first is first in flight."

Another said:

"Do not cut off a friend as long as your eyes glance, from the words of a hateful, wicked enemy; and do not tire of visiting him: visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: repetition is to drive away heedlessness and to affirm the proof.

Then he stood at the maqam and said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious, who taught the Qur'an," raising his voice with it, while the Quraysh were in their assemblies. They paid attention and said: "What is the son of Umm Abd saying?" Then they rose toward him and began beating him while he kept reciting, until he reached what he reached of it. Then he returned to his Companions, and they had left marks on his face. They said: "This is what we feared for you."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The Most Gracious, who taught the Qur'an. It was revealed when they said: "What is the Most Gracious?" It was also said: it is an answer to the people of Mecca when they said: "It is only a human being who teaches him" (Q. 16:103).

It was also said: He taught him all languages; Adam, peace be upon him, spoke seven hundred thousand languages, the best of which was Arabic. Others said: it refers to all people, because "man" (al-insan) is a generic noun. Then they differed about the meaning of al-bayan. It is narrated from Qatada that he said: He taught him the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful, and made clear to him good and evil, and what to do and what to leave, so that He might thereby argue against him.

Abu al-Aliya, Murra al-Hamdani and Ibn Zayd said: it means speech. Al-Hasan said: articulation and discernment. Muhammad ibn Ka'b: what one says and what is said to him. Al-Suddi: He taught every people the tongue with which they speak. Yaman: writing and script with the pen; its parallel is "He taught by the pen" (Q. 96:4). Ibn Kaysan said: "Created man" means Muhammad (ﷺ), "taught him expression" means the explanation of what was and what will be, because he explained about the first and the last and about the Day of Judgment.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan said: by them is meant the reckoning of times, lifespans and terms. Were it not for night, day, the sun and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything. The nominative of "the sun and the moon" is by supposing a verb whose sense is: "the sun and the moon run by a reckoning." It was also said: it is a subject whose predicate is what follows.

The structure of the verse: "The Most Gracious taught the Qur'an" and "[He] determined the sun and the moon." It was also said: it is connected to "expression," meaning: He taught him expression, [and] that the sun and the moon are by a reckoning.

It is said: the extent of the sun is six thousand four hundred farsakhs in the like of it, and the extent of the moon is a thousand farsakhs by a thousand farsakhs.

It is written on the face of the sun: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; He created the sun by His power and set it running by His command." And on its belly is written: "There is no god but Allah. His pleasure is speech, His anger is speech, His mercy is speech, His punishment is speech." On the face of the moon is written: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; Allah created the moon, and created the darknesses and the light." And on its belly is written: "There is no god but Allah. He created good and evil by His power, by which He tests whom He wills of His creation. Blessed is the one through whose hands Allah makes good flow, and woe to the one through whose hands Allah makes evil flow."

And the star and the tree prostrate (yasjudan). It was said: it is what has no stem among trees and spreads over the face of the earth. Al-Suddi said: it is the collective term for plants; it was called a star (najm) because it rises (tala') from the earth, and their prostration is the prostration of their shadows. Mujahid and Qatada said: it is the constellation, and its prostration is its rising.

And the heaven, He raised it and set the balance (al-mizan). Mujahid said: justice. Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: it is that by which weighing is done, so that fairness and redress are attained. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the Qur'an. The root of weighing (al-wazn) is measurement.

That you not transgress (alla tatghaw) in the balance, meaning: lest you incline and wrong and exceed the truth in the balance. Establish the weight with justice (bi-l-qist), that is, with equity. Abu al-Darda said: set up the tongue of the balance with justice. Ibn Uyayna said: the establishing is with the hand, and the justice is with the heart. And do not make the balance deficient (la tukhsiru), that is, do not diminish the balance, and do not cheat in measure and weight.

Qatada said on this verse: "Be just, son of Adam, as you wish to be dealt with justly; and give full measure as you wish to be given full measure, for justice is the wellbeing of people."

The common reading is tukhsiru with a dammed ta' and a kasra on the sin. Bilal ibn Abi Burda read it with a fatha on the ta' and a kasra on the sin; both are dialectal forms.

And the earth, He laid it down for the creatures (lil-anam): for the created beings. Al-Hasan said: for jinn and humans. Ibn Abbas and al-Sha'bi said: for every living soul.

In it are fruits (fakiha). That is, the varieties of fruit. Ibn Kaysan said: that is what delights them with the uncounted blessings, and every blessing is a delight.

And the palm trees with sheaths (akmam): the containers of dates. Its singular is kumm; everything that covers us is a kumm and a kumma, and from it comes "kumm al-qamis" (the sleeve of a shirt). It is also said that a cap is called kumma. The poet said:

Al-Dahhak said: "dhat al-akmam" means possessing sheaths. Al-Hasan: its akmam are its fibres. Qatada: its necks. Ibn Zayd: the spathe before it splits open.

And the grain with its husk (al-habb dhu al-asf). Mujahid said: it is the leaves of the crop. Ibn al-Sikkit said: the Arabs call the leaves of the crop: al-asf, al-asifa and al-jull (with a kasra on the jim). Alqama ibn Abda said:

Then he stood at the maqam and said: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Most Gracious, who taught the Qur'an," raising his voice with it, while the Quraysh were in their assemblies. They paid attention and said: "What is the son of Umm Abd saying?" Then they rose toward him and began beating him while he kept reciting, until he reached what he reached of it. Then he returned to his Companions, and they had left marks on his face. They said: "This is what we feared for you."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Created man. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: this means Adam, peace be upon him.

It was also said: He taught him all languages; Adam, peace be upon him, spoke seven hundred thousand languages, the best of which was Arabic. Others said: it refers to all people, because "man" (al-insan) is a generic noun. Then they differed about the meaning of al-bayan. Ibn Kaysan said: "Created man" means Muhammad (ﷺ), "taught him expression" means the explanation of what was and what will be, because he explained about the first and the last and about the Day of Judgment.

The people of Kufa, except Asim, read "wa al-rayhani" in the genitive, in coordination with "al-asf."

So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny (fa-bi-ayyi ala'i rabbikuma tukadhdhiban), O you two jinn and humankind.

Evidence for this is what

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muslim al-Hanbali narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Khaliq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ibrahim al-Tarjumani narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Ammar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to us Surat al-Rahman until he finished it. Then he said: "What is wrong with you that I see you silent? The jinn gave a better response than you. Whenever I recited this verse to them, 'So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' they said: 'None of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny.'" [165] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/325, no. 4146.]]

It is also said: He addressed them with the dual form, according to the custom of the Arabs; this question has already passed in His saying: "Cast into Hell" (Q. 50:24).

As for the wisdom of its repetition, al-Qutaybi said: Allah, glorified and exalted, enumerated His blessings in this surah and reminded His creatures of His favours. Then He followed the mention of each word He established and each blessing He mentioned with this verse, making it a separator between every two blessings, to alert them to the blessings and to affirm them. It is like your saying to a man: "I did good to him and followed it with gifts," while he denies you and disbelieves you: "Were you not poor and I enriched you? Will you deny this? Were you not naked and I clothed you? Will you deny this? Did I not carry you when you were riding? Will you deny this? Were you not obscure and I honoured you? Will you deny this? Were you not a celibate and I brought you to pilgrimage? Will you deny this?"

Repetition is permissible in Arab speech and is good in such a place. The poet said:

"..."

Another said:

"How many blessings were yours, how many, how many, and how many."

Another said:

"Fazara's party almost roasted us, so Fazara's first is first in flight."

Another said:

"Do not cut off a friend as long as your eyes glance, from the words of a hateful, wicked enemy; and do not tire of visiting him: visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him, visit him."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: repetition is to drive away heedlessness and to affirm the proof.

Al-Husayn also informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama told us, saying: Sa'id al-Jazari told us, on the authority of one who heard al-Lajlaj say: I heard Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who was his brother and friend, say: I heard him say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed by a man praying and he was saying: "O Owner of Majesty and Honour!" Al-Husayn also informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib al-Masisi told us, saying: Hilal ibn al-'Ala' told us, saying: Abu al-Jarrar told us, saying: 'Ammar ibn Zuraiq told us, from al-A'mash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: 'O Owner of Majesty and Honour!'" [Musnad Ahmad: 4/177.]

It was called out to him: "I have heard. What is your need?"

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾, from angels, humans, jinn and others; none of them is without need of Him. Ibn 'Abbas said: the people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness and do not ask Him for provision, while the people of the earth ask Him for provision and forgiveness.

﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾. Muqatil said: this was revealed concerning the Jews when they said: "God does not decree anything on the Sabbath," so God, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hawzi informed me, saying: Abu Ahmad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Adi, the memorizer of hadith, informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Tuwayt Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Bakr told us, saying: Harith ibn 'Ubayda ibn Riyah al-Ghassani told us, from his father, from 'Ubayda ibn Abi Riyah, from Muthbit ibn 'Abd Allah al-Azdi, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Munib, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited to us this verse: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾. We said: "O Messenger of God, what is that affair?" He said: "He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people and lowers others." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/117.]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abduws told us by dictation, saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Bazzaz informed us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Rabi' al-Makki told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna told us, saying: Abu Hamza al-Thumali told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Among what God, Exalted and Glorified, created is a tablet of white pearl, its two covers are red ruby, its pen is light and its writing is light. God, Exalted is He, looks into it every day three hundred and sixty glances: He creates, provides, gives life, causes death, honours, humbles, and does what He wills. That is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾.

Mujahid and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: among His affairs is that He answers one who calls, gives to one who asks, releases a captive, heals a sick person, forgives a sin and turns in repentance to a people. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: all time is, in God's sight, two days: one is the duration of the days of this world, and the other is the Day of Resurrection. The affair in which He is during the day that is the duration of this world is testing through command and prohibition, giving life and causing death, giving and withholding. The affair of the Day of Resurrection is recompense, reckoning, reward and punishment. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is driving the decrees toward their appointed times.

It is also said: His affair, Exalted is He, is that He goes forth every day and night with three armies: an army from the loins of fathers to the wombs, an army from the wombs into this world, and an army from this world to the graves; then they all return to God, Exalted is He. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: He creates a people, causes others to die, and provides for them and protects them. Suwayd ibn Jabala al-Farari said: He frees necks, relieves hardships and gives generously to those who desire. Some said: it is gathering and separating. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: it is His delivering benefits to you and warding off harms from you. So how shall we be heedless of obedience to One who is never heedless of us? He also said: in this verse, "every day" there is for His servants a new kindness.

It is related that a certain ruler asked his vizier about the meaning of this verse, and the vizier did not know it, and asked for a delay until the next day. The vizier returned to his house in sorrow, and a black slave of his said to him: "My lord, what has befallen you?" He rebuked him.

He said: "My lord, tell me, perhaps God, Exalted is He, will make relief easy for you through my hands." So he told him about it, and he said to him: "Go back to the ruler and say to him: I have a black slave; if you permit him, he will explain this verse to you." He did so, and the ruler summoned the slave and asked him about it. He said: "Your Honour, the affair of God is that He ﴿causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night﴾, and ﴿brings the dead out of the living and brings the living out of the dead﴾, and heals the sick, and makes the healthy ill, and tests the well and grants wellbeing to the tested, and exalts the humbled and humbles the exalted, and makes the poor rich and the rich poor." The ruler said: "Well done, boy, you have relieved me." Then he ordered the vizier to take off the robes of the office, and he clothed the slave in them. He said: "My lord, this is the affair of God, Mighty and Majestic."

But it is permitted in the speech of the Arabs to mention two things and then attribute an action to only one of them, like the saying of God, Exalted is He: ﴿O assembly of jinn and men, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ The messengers were from mankind, not from the jinn, as al-Kalbi said. He also said: ﴿and He placed the moon therein as a light﴾, though it is in only one of them.

Some said: pearls come out of the rain water and sea water. The pearl is greater than the *durr*, and its singular is *lu'lu'a*. ﴿And coral﴾ is its small ones. Once it was said: coral is the fine pearl. Al-Suddi reported from Abu Malik that coral is red beads. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said it is *al-basdh*, a red jewel; it was also said that it is small pearls. Ibn Mas'ud's saying supports this: "Coral is a stone." What we have related, that the two seas are the land and the sea, and that the pronoun in "*minhuma*" refers to both, is the saying of al-Dahhak, and the report of 'Atiyya from Ibn 'Abbas, and Layth from Mujahid.

In confirmation of this, Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Lu'lu' told us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi told us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who recited "*yakhruju minhuma al-lu'lu' wal-marjan*" and said: when the sky rains, the shells open their mouths, and wherever a drop falls, it becomes a pearl.

It was also mentioned to me that a date stone was inside a shell; some of the stone was struck by a drop and some was not, so where the drop struck the stone it became a pearl, and the rest remained a stone.

Al-Husayn informed us, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: my father read to Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Alawayh al-Qattan from his book while I was listening, saying: some of our companions told us, saying: a man from Egypt called Tasm told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, from his father, from Sufyan al-Thawri, regarding God's saying, Exalted is He, ﴿He released the two seas meeting, between them a barrier they do not transgress﴾: he said: "Fatima and 'Ali." ﴿From both of them come pearls and coral﴾: he said: "al-Hasan and al-Husayn." [Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/143, at the verse.]

This saying was also reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is Muhammad (ﷺ). And God knows best. [The previous source.]

The people of allusion (*ahl al-ishara*, those who interpret the Qur'an through inner indications) said: ﴿He released the two seas﴾: one of them is the knowledge of the heart, and the second is the disobedience of the soul; ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is the mercy and protection.

﴿They do not transgress﴾: the disobedience of the soul does not affect the knowledge of the heart. Ibn 'Ata' said: between the servant and the Lord there are two seas. One is the sea of salvation, which is the Qur'an; whoever clings to it is saved. The second is the sea of destruction, which is this world; whoever holds to it and leans on it is destroyed. It was also said: the sea of this world and the sea of the Hereafter. ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is the grave, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿and behind them is a barrier until the day they are resurrected﴾.

﴿They do not transgress﴾: neither of them encroaches upon the other. It was also said: the sea of reason and the ssea of desire. ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is the kindness of God, Exalted is He. ﴿From them come pearls and coral﴾: the divine success and protection. It was also said: the sea of life and the sea of death; ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is the appointed term. It was also said: the sea of proof and the sea of doubt; ﴿between them a barrier﴾ is reflection and inference; ﴿from them come pearls and coral﴾: the truth and the correct.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

﴿And His are the ships, the lofty ones, sailing on the sea like mountains﴾. *Al-Munshaʼat* with a *kasra* on its *sin* was read by Hamza, and it is the narration of al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, meaning those that come forward, beginning with their running and their course. The others read it with a *fatha*, meaning the created things that are raised up and subjected.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

﴿Everyone upon it is passing away﴾, that is, upon the earth, of living creatures. This is a reference to something not mentioned, like the saying of people, "*ma 'alayha akram min fulan*" ("nothing on it is more honourable than so-and-so"), meaning the earth, and "*wa ma bayna labatayha afdal minhu*" meaning the two sides of Medina. ﴿perishes﴾, destroyed. Ibn 'Abbas said: when this verse was revealed, the angels said: "The people of the earth have perished." So God, Exalted is He, revealed ﴿Everything perishes except His face﴾, and the angels were then certain of destruction.

﴿And there remains the face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾. The common reading is with *waw*. 'Abd Allah read *dhi al-jalal* with *ya'*, as an attribute of the Lord.

Al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abd Allah informed me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kinani told us, saying: al-Harith ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman al-Waqqasi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for me and said: "O Ibn Salam, God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾. As for honour, you know it, but what is majesty?"

He said: "By my father, you are! We find in the books that it is the Garden that encompasses the Throne." He said: "How far is it between it and the gardens in which God settles His servants?" He said: "The distance of seven hundred years." He said: "Then Gabriel came down with its confirmation." [No discerning reader can miss in this report the fabrication, the belittling and the plot against Islam and its Prophet, for how could it be conceived that the Prophet of Islam would ask about a matter that had become unclear to him from a Jewish man, 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, without seeking help from Gabriel (peace be upon him)? God says in His clear revelation: ﴿Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification﴾.]

Al-Husayn also informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ibn Mahan told us, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama told us, saying: Sa'id al-Jazari told us, on the authority of one who heard al-Lajlaj say: I heard Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who was his brother and friend, say: I heard him say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed by a man praying and he was saying: "O Owner of Majesty and Honour!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Your request has been granted." [Musnad Ahmad: 5/236.]

Al-Husayn also informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khasib al-Masisi told us, saying: Hilal ibn al-'Ala' told us, saying: Abu al-Jarrar told us, saying: 'Ammar ibn Zuraiq told us, from al-A'mash, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: 'O Owner of Majesty and Honour!'" [Musnad Ahmad: 4/177.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Saqlab told us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Khasib told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yunus told us, from Bisr ibn 'Umar, who said: Wuhayb ibn Khalid told us, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, who said: A man performed the pilgrimage, and he sat calling out: "O Owner of Majesty and Honour!" It was called out to him: "I have heard. What is your need?"

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾, from angels, humans, jinn and others; none of them is without need of Him. Ibn 'Abbas said: the people of the heavens ask Him for forgiveness and do not ask Him for provision, while the people of the earth ask Him for provision and forgiveness.

﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾. Muqatil said: this was revealed concerning the Jews when they said: "God does not decree anything on the Sabbath," so God, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾.

Abu al-Qasim 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hawzi informed me, saying: Abu Ahmad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Adi, the memorizer of hadith, informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Tuwayt Abu al-Qasim al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi told us, saying: 'Umar ibn Bakr told us, saying: Harith ibn 'Ubayda ibn Riyah al-Ghassani told us, from his father, from 'Ubayda ibn Abi Riyah, from Muthbit ibn 'Abd Allah al-Azdi, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Munib, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited to us this verse: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾. We said: "O Messenger of God, what is that affair?" He said: "He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people and lowers others." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/117.]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abduws told us by dictation, saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Bazzaz informed us, saying: Yahya ibn al-Rabi' al-Makki told us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna told us, saying: Abu Hamza al-Thumali told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Among what God, Exalted and Glorified, created is a tablet of white pearl, its two covers are red ruby, its pen is light and its writing is light. God, Exalted is He, looks into it every day three hundred and sixty glances: He creates, provides, gives life, causes death, honours, humbles, and does what He wills. That is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Every day He is upon some affair﴾.

Mujahid and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: among His affairs is that He answers one who calls, gives to one who asks, releases a captive, heals a sick person, forgives a sin and turns in repentance to a people. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: all time is, in God's sight, two days: one is the duration of the days of this world, and the other is the Day of Resurrection. The affair in which He is during the day that is the duration of this world is testing through command and prohibition, giving life and causing death, giving and withholding. The affair of the Day of Resurrection is recompense, reckoning, reward and punishment. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is driving the decrees toward their appointed times.

It is also said: His affair, Exalted is He, is that He goes forth every day and night with three armies: an army from the loins of fathers to the wombs, an army from the wombs into this world, and an army from this world to the graves; then they all return to God, Exalted is He. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: He creates a people, causes others to die, and provides for them and protects them. Suwayd ibn Jabala al-Farari said: He frees necks, relieves hardships and gives generously to those who desire. Some said: it is gathering and separating. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: it is His delivering benefits to you and warding off harms from you. So how shall we be heedless of obedience to One who is never heedless of us? He also said: in this verse, "every day" there is for His servants a new kindness.

It is related that a certain ruler asked his vizier about the meaning of this verse, and the vizier did not know it, and asked for a delay until the next day. The vizier returned to his house in sorrow, and a black slave of his said to him: "My lord, what has befallen you?" He rebuked him.

He said: "My lord, tell me, perhaps God, Exalted is He, will make relief easy for you through my hands." So he told him about it, and he said to him: "Go back to the ruler and say to him: I have a black slave; if you permit him, he will explain this verse to you." He did so, and the ruler summoned the slave and asked him about it. He said: "Your Honour, the affair of God is that He ﴿causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night﴾, and ﴿brings the dead out of the living and brings the living out of the dead﴾, and heals the sick, and makes the healthy ill, and tests the well and grants wellbeing to the tested, and exalts the humbled and humbles the exalted, and makes the poor rich and the rich poor." The ruler said: "Well done, boy, you have relieved me." Then he ordered the vizier to take off the robes of the office, and he clothed the slave in them. He said: "My lord, this is the affair of God, Mighty and Majestic."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 55, verses 31–38:**

﴿Soon We will attend to you, O two worlds (sananfughu lakum).﴾ ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) and Ubayy read *sanafrughu ilaykum* ("Soon We will attend to you"). Al-Aʿmash read *sa-yufrighu* with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ*, without naming the subject. Al-Aʿraj read it with a *fatḥa* on the *nūn* and the *rāʾ*. Al-Kisaʾi said: this is the dialect of Tamim. Ḥamza, al-Kisaʾi and Khalaf read with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ*, and Abu ʿUbayd preferred this reading, by analogy with His words ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾ (55:29), so that "the report follows the report." The rest read with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ* and a *ḍamma* on the *rāʾ*, and Abu Ḥatim preferred this.

It may be said: "Leisure (*farāgh*) only comes from being occupied, and God, exalted is He, is not preoccupied by one matter over another." We say:

The scholars differed about the meaning of this verse. Some said: this is a warning and threat from God, exalted is He, to them, like the speaker who says, "I will certainly make time for you," while he has no occupation. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥak. Others said: its meaning is "We will certainly turn to you after leaving you and delaying, and We will begin your affair." A speaker may say to one who has no occupation, "You have freed yourself for me" (*faraghta lī*) and "I have freed myself for my insulting him," meaning: I began it and turned to it. Jarir ibn al-Khatafi said:

*When the Iraqi smith met his rear,*
*I turned to the shackled smith (his rival) with what would grieve him.*

That is: I aimed at him with what would distress him. This view was preferred by al-Fanadi and al-Kisaʾi.

Some said: God, exalted is He, promised reward for piety and threatened for wickedness, then said, ﴿We will attend to you﴾ regarding what We have threatened and informed you of, so We will call you to account and recompense you, and fulfil for you what We promised and bring each to what We have appointed, and that will be completed and finished. This is the view of al-Hasan, Muqatil and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Kaysan said: *al-farāgh* to an act is to devote oneself to it to the exclusion of others.

﴿O you two worlds﴾ (*ayyuhā al-thaqalān*), that is, the jinn and mankind. The evidence for this is His words after it, ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind﴾ (55:33). They were called *thaqalān* (the two weighty ones) because they are a weight upon the earth, living and dead. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ (99:2). Some scholars of meanings said: everything of worth that people compete for is a *thiql* (weight), and from this the eggs of the ostrich were called *thiql*, because the one who finds and hunts them rejoices when he obtains them. The poet said:

*So they remembered a heavy, precious thing, after
the ostrich had put its right claw into a sand-hole.*

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of God and my family (ʿitrah)." So he called them two weighty things, glorifying their station. Jaʿfar al-Sadiq said: the jinn and mankind were called *thaqalān* because they are weighed down by sins.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:34). ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ (55:33). He did not say "you two are able" (*istaṭaʿtumā*) because they are two groups, in the plural sense, as in His words, ﴿and behold, they are two groups disputing﴾ (22:19), and His words, ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ (22:19).

﴿To pass through the regions (*aqṭār*)﴾, that is, to pass beyond them, of the heavens and the earth, that is, their sides (*aṭrāf*). ﴿Then pass through﴾. The meaning of the verse: if you are able to cross the sides of the heavens and the earth, so as to escape your Lord and make Him unable to seize you, then cross over. This is said to them on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it means fleeing from death, so He informs that no one can protect them from death and that they have no escape from it. Even if they passed through the regions of the heavens and the earth, they would still be under the authority and dominion of God, mighty and majestic. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means, if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it, but you will not know it except by authority, meaning clear proof from God, exalted is He. ﴿You will not pass except by authority﴾, that is, by proof (*ḥujja*).

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAṭāʾ said: you will not get out of His authority. It was also said the meaning is "except to My authority," like His words, ﴿and He was good to me﴾ (12:100), meaning He was good to me. The poet said:

*You harmed us, so be good to us; there is no blame
in us, nor are we hateful, if she becomes estranged.*

It is reported in a report: "The angels will surround the creation, and with them a tongue of fire; then they will be called: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able...﴾ ..." That is His saying, exalted is He ...

﴿A flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾ (55:35). Ibn Kathir and Ibn Abi Ishaq read *shuwāẓ* with a *kasra* on the *shīn*, while the others read it with a *ḍamma*. Both are dialects, like *ṣiwār* and *ṣuwār* for a herd of cattle. *Shuwāẓ* is the flame. Ḥassan ibn Thabit, satirizing Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt, said:

*I satirized you, so you were humbled in disgrace,
with a rhyme blazing like flames.*

Ru'bah said:

*Among them, from our encounter, are prostrations (*aqyāṣ*)
and the fire of war that kindles the flames.*

Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it is the smoke that comes out of the flame, not the smoke of firewood.

﴿And brass (*nuḥās*)﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read it with a *kasra* on the *sīn*, as a conjunction to *al-nār* (fire), and Abu Ḥatim preferred this. The rest read it with a *ḍamma*, as a conjunction to *shuwāẓ*, and Abu ʿUbayd preferred this.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: *al-nuḥās* is smoke. This is also the report of Abu Ṣalih and Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Nabigha said:

*It shines like the light of a lamp of sesame oil,
God has not placed brass (smoke) in it.*

Al-Aṣmaʿi said: I heard a Bedouin say: *al-saliṭ* is the fat of the hump, and it has no smoke. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is molten brass (*ṣafr*) poured over their heads. This is the report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. Muqatil said: they are five rivers of molten brass flowing from beneath the Throne over the heads of the people of the Fire: three rivers for the length of the night and two rivers for the length of the day. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: *nuḥās* is *muhl* (dregs of molten metal). Rabiʿ said: it is pitch (*qaṭr*). Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it is the sediment of oil. Al-Kisaʾi said: it is that which has a strong smell.

﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves (*fa-lā tantaṣirān*)﴾, that is, you will not be able to avenge yourselves and you will be prevented.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:37). ﴿And when the sky is split open (*fa-idhā inshaqqat*)﴾, that is, it is split apart (*infaraǵat*), and so it becomes gates for the descent of the angels. Its explanation is His words, ﴿on the Day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in procession﴾ (25:25). ﴿And it became (*fa-kānat*)﴾, that is, it became, ﴿a rose (*wardatan*)﴾, bright; it was also said: changing; and it was also said: the colour of a rose.

Qatadah said: today it is green, but on that day it will have another colour. ﴿Like red leather (*kal-dihān*)﴾. The scholars differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḍaḥḥak, Qatadah and al-Rabiʿ said: it means like the colour of the rose, which in spring is reddish-yellow, and when the first winter cold strikes it, it becomes reddish-red, and when winter intensifies it becomes reddish-dusty. So the sky, in its changing colours when it is split, is compared to this rose in its changing colours. Mujahid and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: like oil (*duhn*), and this is the report of Shaybān from Qatadah. He said: *al-dihān* is the plural of *duhn*, and oil has colours, and he likened the sky to its colours. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah said: like the juice of olive oil, changing colours in an hour. Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: like the flowing of oil, changing colour. Ibn Jurayj said: the sky melts like molten oil, when the heat of Hell strikes it. Muqatil said: like pure rose oil. Muʾarrikh said: like a red rose. Al-Kalbi said: like red leather, and its plural is *adhina*.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: Luqman al-Ḥanafi related to us, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a young man in the middle of the night who was reciting this verse: ﴿And when the sky is split open and becomes a rose, like red leather﴾. The young man stopped, and tears choked him, and he began to say: "Woe to me, on a day when the sky will be split open, woe to me!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young man, like it, or the likeness of it. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the angels have wept, O young man, because of your weeping."

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: *al-nuḥās* is smoke. This is also the report of Abu Ṣalih and Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Nabigha said:

*It shines like the light of a lamp of sesame oil,
God has not placed brass (smoke) in it.*

Al-Aṣmaʿi said: I heard a Bedouin say: *al-saliṭ* is the fat of the hump, and it has no smoke. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is molten brass (*ṣafr*) poured over their heads. This is the report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. Muqatil said: they are five rivers of molten brass flowing from beneath the Throne over the heads of the people of the Fire: three rivers for the length of the night and two rivers for the length of the day. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: *nuḥās* is *muhl* (dregs of molten metal). Rabiʿ said: it is pitch (*qaṭr*). Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it is the sediment of oil. Al-Kisaʾi said: it is that which has a strong smell.

﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves (*fa-lā tantaṣirān*)﴾, that is, you will not be able to avenge yourselves and you will be prevented.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:37). ﴿And when the sky is split open (*fa-idhā inshaqqat*)﴾, that is, it is split apart (*infaraǵat*), and so it becomes gates for the descent of the angels. Its explanation is His words, ﴿on the Day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in procession﴾ (25:25). ﴿And it became (*fa-kānat*)﴾, that is, it became, ﴿a rose (*wardatan*)﴾, bright; it was also said: changing; and it was also said: the colour of a rose.

Qatadah said: today it is green, but on that day it will have another colour. ﴿Like red leather (*kal-dihān*)﴾. The scholars differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḍaḥḥak, Qatadah and al-Rabiʿ said: it means like the colour of the rose, which in spring is reddish-yellow, and when the first winter cold strikes it, it becomes reddish-red, and when winter intensifies it becomes reddish-dusty. So the sky, in its changing colours when it is split, is compared to this rose in its changing colours. Mujahid and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: like oil (*duhn*), and this is the report of Shaybān from Qatadah. He said: *al-dihān* is the plural of *duhn*, and oil has colours, and he likened the sky to its colours. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah said: like the juice of olive oil, changing colours in an hour. Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: like the flowing of oil, changing colour. Ibn Jurayj said: the sky melts like molten oil, when the heat of Hell strikes it. Muqatil said: like pure rose oil. Muʾarrikh said: like a red rose. Al-Kalbi said: like red leather, and its plural is *adhina*.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: Luqman al-Ḥanafi related to us, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a young man in the middle of the night who was reciting this verse: ﴿And when the sky is split open and becomes a rose, like red leather﴾. The young man stopped, and tears choked him, and he began to say: "Woe to me, on a day when the sky will be split open, woe to me!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young man, like it, or the likeness of it. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the angels have wept, O young man, because of your weeping."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 55, verses 31–38:**

﴿Soon We will attend to you, O two worlds (sananfughu lakum).﴾ ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud) and Ubayy read *sanafrughu ilaykum* ("Soon We will attend to you"). Al-Aʿmash read *sa-yufrighu* with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ*, without naming the subject. Al-Aʿraj read it with a *fatḥa* on the *nūn* and the *rāʾ*. Al-Kisaʾi said: this is the dialect of Tamim. Ḥamza, al-Kisaʾi and Khalaf read with a *ḍamma* on the *yāʾ* and a *fatḥa* on the *rāʾ*, and Abu ʿUbayd preferred this reading, by analogy with His words ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him﴾ (55:29), so that "the report follows the report." The rest read with a *fatḥa* on the *yāʾ* and a *ḍamma* on the *rāʾ*, and Abu Ḥatim preferred this.

It may be said: "Leisure (*farāgh*) only comes from being occupied, and God, exalted is He, is not preoccupied by one matter over another." We say:

The scholars differed about the meaning of this verse. Some said: this is a warning and threat from God, exalted is He, to them, like the speaker who says, "I will certainly make time for you," while he has no occupation. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Ḍaḥḥak. Others said: its meaning is "We will certainly turn to you after leaving you and delaying, and We will begin your affair." A speaker may say to one who has no occupation, "You have freed yourself for me" (*faraghta lī*) and "I have freed myself for my insulting him," meaning: I began it and turned to it. Jarir ibn al-Khatafi said:

*When the Iraqi smith met his rear,*
*I turned to the shackled smith (his rival) with what would grieve him.*

That is: I aimed at him with what would distress him. This view was preferred by al-Fanadi and al-Kisaʾi.

Some said: God, exalted is He, promised reward for piety and threatened for wickedness, then said, ﴿We will attend to you﴾ regarding what We have threatened and informed you of, so We will call you to account and recompense you, and fulfil for you what We promised and bring each to what We have appointed, and that will be completed and finished. This is the view of al-Hasan, Muqatil and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Kaysan said: *al-farāgh* to an act is to devote oneself to it to the exclusion of others.

﴿O you two worlds﴾ (*ayyuhā al-thaqalān*), that is, the jinn and mankind. The evidence for this is His words after it, ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind﴾ (55:33). They were called *thaqalān* (the two weighty ones) because they are a weight upon the earth, living and dead. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ (99:2). Some scholars of meanings said: everything of worth that people compete for is a *thiql* (weight), and from this the eggs of the ostrich were called *thiql*, because the one who finds and hunts them rejoices when he obtains them. The poet said:

*So they remembered a heavy, precious thing, after
the ostrich had put its right claw into a sand-hole.*

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am leaving among you the two weighty things: the Book of God and my family (ʿitrah)." So he called them two weighty things, glorifying their station. Jaʿfar al-Sadiq said: the jinn and mankind were called *thaqalān* because they are weighed down by sins.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:34). ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through; you will not pass except with authority﴾ (55:33). He did not say "you two are able" (*istaṭaʿtumā*) because they are two groups, in the plural sense, as in His words, ﴿and behold, they are two groups disputing﴾ (22:19), and His words, ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord﴾ (22:19).

﴿To pass through the regions (*aqṭār*)﴾, that is, to pass beyond them, of the heavens and the earth, that is, their sides (*aṭrāf*). ﴿Then pass through﴾. The meaning of the verse: if you are able to cross the sides of the heavens and the earth, so as to escape your Lord and make Him unable to seize you, then cross over. This is said to them on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it means fleeing from death, so He informs that no one can protect them from death and that they have no escape from it. Even if they passed through the regions of the heavens and the earth, they would still be under the authority and dominion of God, mighty and majestic. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means, if you are able to know what is in the heavens and the earth, then know it, but you will not know it except by authority, meaning clear proof from God, exalted is He. ﴿You will not pass except by authority﴾, that is, by proof (*ḥujja*).

Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAṭāʾ said: you will not get out of His authority. It was also said the meaning is "except to My authority," like His words, ﴿and He was good to me﴾ (12:100), meaning He was good to me. The poet said:

*You harmed us, so be good to us; there is no blame
in us, nor are we hateful, if she becomes estranged.*

It is reported in a report: "The angels will surround the creation, and with them a tongue of fire; then they will be called: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able...﴾ ..." That is His saying, exalted is He ...

﴿A flame of fire will be sent against you both﴾ (55:35). Ibn Kathir and Ibn Abi Ishaq read *shuwāẓ* with a *kasra* on the *shīn*, while the others read it with a *ḍamma*. Both are dialects, like *ṣiwār* and *ṣuwār* for a herd of cattle. *Shuwāẓ* is the flame. Ḥassan ibn Thabit, satirizing Umayyah ibn Abi al-Ṣalt, said:

*I satirized you, so you were humbled in disgrace,
with a rhyme blazing like flames.*

Ru'bah said:

*Among them, from our encounter, are prostrations (*aqyāṣ*)
and the fire of war that kindles the flames.*

Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it is the smoke that comes out of the flame, not the smoke of firewood.

﴿And brass (*nuḥās*)﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read it with a *kasra* on the *sīn*, as a conjunction to *al-nār* (fire), and Abu Ḥatim preferred this. The rest read it with a *ḍamma*, as a conjunction to *shuwāẓ*, and Abu ʿUbayd preferred this.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: *al-nuḥās* is smoke. This is also the report of Abu Ṣalih and Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Nabigha said:

*It shines like the light of a lamp of sesame oil,
God has not placed brass (smoke) in it.*

Al-Aṣmaʿi said: I heard a Bedouin say: *al-saliṭ* is the fat of the hump, and it has no smoke. Mujahid and Qatadah said: it is molten brass (*ṣafr*) poured over their heads. This is the report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. Muqatil said: they are five rivers of molten brass flowing from beneath the Throne over the heads of the people of the Fire: three rivers for the length of the night and two rivers for the length of the day. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said: *nuḥās* is *muhl* (dregs of molten metal). Rabiʿ said: it is pitch (*qaṭr*). Al-Ḍaḥḥak said: it is the sediment of oil. Al-Kisaʾi said: it is that which has a strong smell.

﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves (*fa-lā tantaṣirān*)﴾, that is, you will not be able to avenge yourselves and you will be prevented.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾ (55:37). ﴿And when the sky is split open (*fa-idhā inshaqqat*)﴾, that is, it is split apart (*infaraǵat*), and so it becomes gates for the descent of the angels. Its explanation is His words, ﴿on the Day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in procession﴾ (25:25). ﴿And it became (*fa-kānat*)﴾, that is, it became, ﴿a rose (*wardatan*)﴾, bright; it was also said: changing; and it was also said: the colour of a rose.

Qatadah said: today it is green, but on that day it will have another colour. ﴿Like red leather (*kal-dihān*)﴾. The scholars differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Ḍaḥḥak, Qatadah and al-Rabiʿ said: it means like the colour of the rose, which in spring is reddish-yellow, and when the first winter cold strikes it, it becomes reddish-red, and when winter intensifies it becomes reddish-dusty. So the sky, in its changing colours when it is split, is compared to this rose in its changing colours. Mujahid and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: like oil (*duhn*), and this is the report of Shaybān from Qatadah. He said: *al-dihān* is the plural of *duhn*, and oil has colours, and he likened the sky to its colours. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah said: like the juice of olive oil, changing colours in an hour. Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl said: like the flowing of oil, changing colour. Ibn Jurayj said: the sky melts like molten oil, when the heat of Hell strikes it. Muqatil said: like pure rose oil. Muʾarrikh said: like a red rose. Al-Kalbi said: like red leather, and its plural is *adhina*.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah related to us, saying: Ibn Ayyub related to us, saying: Luqman al-Ḥanafi related to us, saying: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a young man in the middle of the night who was reciting this verse: ﴿And when the sky is split open and becomes a rose, like red leather﴾. The young man stopped, and tears choked him, and he began to say: "Woe to me, on a day when the sky will be split open, woe to me!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young man, like it, or the likeness of it. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the angels have wept, O young man, because of your weeping."

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.

﴿Two gardens﴾: two orchards of red ruby and green chrysolite, whose soil is camphor and ambergris, and whose clay is musk of the strongest fragrance. Each orchard is a journey of a hundred years, and in the middle of each orchard is a dwelling of light.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: one garden is for fear of one's Lord, and one garden is for abandoning one's desires. Muqatil said: they are the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: ﴿two gardens﴾ of gold are for the foremost, and two gardens of silver are for the followers.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you know what these two gardens are? They are two orchards among orchards; their foundation is firm, their branches are firm, and their trees are firm."

'Aqil informed me by licence, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us by recitation, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari informed us, saying:

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Hariri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ I said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals, despite the nose of Abu al-Darda' [in the dust]."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Possessing branches [dhawata afnan].﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "afnan" means varieties, its singular being "fann," from the expression "iftanna fulan fi hadithihi" when he takes up its various kinds and forms. Al-Dahhak said: the varieties of fruits.

Mujahid said: branches, its singular being "fann" [or "fanan"]. 'Ikrimah said: the shade of the branches over the walls. Al-Hasan said: "possessing shades," which is like His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾. Al-Dahhak also said: possessing branches and sections. He said: its branches are like trellised vines, touching one another. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: possessing excellence and abundance above all others. Ibn Kaysan said: possessing roots.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: with honour and increase over the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: they flow with pure water, one of them being Tasnim and the other Salsabil.

'Ata'iyyah said: one of them is of water unaltered [by time], and the other is of wine, delicious to those who drink. It was also said: they flow from a mountain of musk. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs﴾ refers to whoever in this world had two eyes that flowed with weeping.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are fruits of every kind, two of each.﴾ Two kinds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world except that it is in Paradise, even the bitter colocynth, except that it is sweet.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on couches [mutaki'in]﴾, a state, ﴿whose linings are of brocade [istabraq]﴾, which is the thick and fine silk. It was also said: it is an Arabized word.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: This is among what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾

He also said: ﴿Its linings are of brocade, and its outer surfaces are of solid light.﴾ Al-Farra' said: by "al-batha'in" he meant the outer surfaces.

The historian said: it is in the language of the Copts, and the lining may be the outer surface and the outer surface the lining, because each of them may be a face. The Arabs say: "this is the back of the sky" and "this is the belly of the sky," for whoever sees it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the killers of 'Uthman: "Allah has killed them in the worst manner, and those of them who escaped fled under the bellies of the stars," meaning they fled by night, so he made the backs of the stars into bellies.

Al-Qutaybi said: this is from the strange interpretations. How can the lining be the outer surface, and the outer surface the lining?

The "batana" is that which is inside of a garment, and it was the custom of people to conceal it, while the "dhiharah" is that which shows, and it is the custom of people to display it. Could anyone say of the face of one praying, "this is its lining," or of what is on the earth's surface, "this is its outer surface"? No, by Allah, that is not permissible. Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.
