Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.

﴿Two gardens﴾: two orchards of red ruby and green chrysolite, whose soil is camphor and ambergris, and whose clay is musk of the strongest fragrance. Each orchard is a journey of a hundred years, and in the middle of each orchard is a dwelling of light.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: one garden is for fear of one's Lord, and one garden is for abandoning one's desires. Muqatil said: they are the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: ﴿two gardens﴾ of gold are for the foremost, and two gardens of silver are for the followers.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you know what these two gardens are? They are two orchards among orchards; their foundation is firm, their branches are firm, and their trees are firm."

'Aqil informed me by licence, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us by recitation, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari informed us, saying:

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Hariri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ I said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals, despite the nose of Abu al-Darda' [in the dust]."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Possessing branches [dhawata afnan].﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "afnan" means varieties, its singular being "fann," from the expression "iftanna fulan fi hadithihi" when he takes up its various kinds and forms. Al-Dahhak said: the varieties of fruits.

Mujahid said: branches, its singular being "fann" [or "fanan"]. 'Ikrimah said: the shade of the branches over the walls. Al-Hasan said: "possessing shades," which is like His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾. Al-Dahhak also said: possessing branches and sections. He said: its branches are like trellised vines, touching one another. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: possessing excellence and abundance above all others. Ibn Kaysan said: possessing roots.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: with honour and increase over the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: they flow with pure water, one of them being Tasnim and the other Salsabil.

'Ata'iyyah said: one of them is of water unaltered [by time], and the other is of wine, delicious to those who drink. It was also said: they flow from a mountain of musk. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs﴾ refers to whoever in this world had two eyes that flowed with weeping.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are fruits of every kind, two of each.﴾ Two kinds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world except that it is in Paradise, even the bitter colocynth, except that it is sweet.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on couches [mutaki'in]﴾, a state, ﴿whose linings are of brocade [istabraq]﴾, which is the thick and fine silk. It was also said: it is an Arabized word.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: This is among what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾

He also said: ﴿Its linings are of brocade, and its outer surfaces are of solid light.﴾ Al-Farra' said: by "al-batha'in" he meant the outer surfaces.

The historian said: it is in the language of the Copts, and the lining may be the outer surface and the outer surface the lining, because each of them may be a face. The Arabs say: "this is the back of the sky" and "this is the belly of the sky," for whoever sees it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the killers of 'Uthman: "Allah has killed them in the worst manner, and those of them who escaped fled under the bellies of the stars," meaning they fled by night, so he made the backs of the stars into bellies.

Al-Qutaybi said: this is from the strange interpretations. How can the lining be the outer surface, and the outer surface the lining?

The "batana" is that which is inside of a garment, and it was the custom of people to conceal it, while the "dhiharah" is that which shows, and it is the custom of people to display it. Could anyone say of the face of one praying, "this is its lining," or of what is on the earth's surface, "this is its outer surface"? No, by Allah, that is not permissible. Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.

﴿Two gardens﴾: two orchards of red ruby and green chrysolite, whose soil is camphor and ambergris, and whose clay is musk of the strongest fragrance. Each orchard is a journey of a hundred years, and in the middle of each orchard is a dwelling of light.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: one garden is for fear of one's Lord, and one garden is for abandoning one's desires. Muqatil said: they are the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: ﴿two gardens﴾ of gold are for the foremost, and two gardens of silver are for the followers.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you know what these two gardens are? They are two orchards among orchards; their foundation is firm, their branches are firm, and their trees are firm."

'Aqil informed me by licence, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us by recitation, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari informed us, saying:

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Hariri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ I said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals, despite the nose of Abu al-Darda' [in the dust]."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Possessing branches [dhawata afnan].﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "afnan" means varieties, its singular being "fann," from the expression "iftanna fulan fi hadithihi" when he takes up its various kinds and forms. Al-Dahhak said: the varieties of fruits.

Mujahid said: branches, its singular being "fann" [or "fanan"]. 'Ikrimah said: the shade of the branches over the walls. Al-Hasan said: "possessing shades," which is like His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾. Al-Dahhak also said: possessing branches and sections. He said: its branches are like trellised vines, touching one another. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: possessing excellence and abundance above all others. Ibn Kaysan said: possessing roots.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: with honour and increase over the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: they flow with pure water, one of them being Tasnim and the other Salsabil.

'Ata'iyyah said: one of them is of water unaltered [by time], and the other is of wine, delicious to those who drink. It was also said: they flow from a mountain of musk. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs﴾ refers to whoever in this world had two eyes that flowed with weeping.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are fruits of every kind, two of each.﴾ Two kinds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world except that it is in Paradise, even the bitter colocynth, except that it is sweet.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on couches [mutaki'in]﴾, a state, ﴿whose linings are of brocade [istabraq]﴾, which is the thick and fine silk. It was also said: it is an Arabized word.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: This is among what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾

He also said: ﴿Its linings are of brocade, and its outer surfaces are of solid light.﴾ Al-Farra' said: by "al-batha'in" he meant the outer surfaces.

The historian said: it is in the language of the Copts, and the lining may be the outer surface and the outer surface the lining, because each of them may be a face. The Arabs say: "this is the back of the sky" and "this is the belly of the sky," for whoever sees it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the killers of 'Uthman: "Allah has killed them in the worst manner, and those of them who escaped fled under the bellies of the stars," meaning they fled by night, so he made the backs of the stars into bellies.

Al-Qutaybi said: this is from the strange interpretations. How can the lining be the outer surface, and the outer surface the lining?

The "batana" is that which is inside of a garment, and it was the custom of people to conceal it, while the "dhiharah" is that which shows, and it is the custom of people to display it. Could anyone say of the face of one praying, "this is its lining," or of what is on the earth's surface, "this is its outer surface"? No, by Allah, that is not permissible. Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.

﴿Two gardens﴾: two orchards of red ruby and green chrysolite, whose soil is camphor and ambergris, and whose clay is musk of the strongest fragrance. Each orchard is a journey of a hundred years, and in the middle of each orchard is a dwelling of light.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: one garden is for fear of one's Lord, and one garden is for abandoning one's desires. Muqatil said: they are the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: ﴿two gardens﴾ of gold are for the foremost, and two gardens of silver are for the followers.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you know what these two gardens are? They are two orchards among orchards; their foundation is firm, their branches are firm, and their trees are firm."

'Aqil informed me by licence, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us by recitation, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari informed us, saying:

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Hariri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ I said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals, despite the nose of Abu al-Darda' [in the dust]."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Possessing branches [dhawata afnan].﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "afnan" means varieties, its singular being "fann," from the expression "iftanna fulan fi hadithihi" when he takes up its various kinds and forms. Al-Dahhak said: the varieties of fruits.

Mujahid said: branches, its singular being "fann" [or "fanan"]. 'Ikrimah said: the shade of the branches over the walls. Al-Hasan said: "possessing shades," which is like His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾. Al-Dahhak also said: possessing branches and sections. He said: its branches are like trellised vines, touching one another. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: possessing excellence and abundance above all others. Ibn Kaysan said: possessing roots.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: with honour and increase over the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: they flow with pure water, one of them being Tasnim and the other Salsabil.

'Ata'iyyah said: one of them is of water unaltered [by time], and the other is of wine, delicious to those who drink. It was also said: they flow from a mountain of musk. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs﴾ refers to whoever in this world had two eyes that flowed with weeping.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are fruits of every kind, two of each.﴾ Two kinds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world except that it is in Paradise, even the bitter colocynth, except that it is sweet.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on couches [mutaki'in]﴾, a state, ﴿whose linings are of brocade [istabraq]﴾, which is the thick and fine silk. It was also said: it is an Arabized word.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: This is among what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾

He also said: ﴿Its linings are of brocade, and its outer surfaces are of solid light.﴾ Al-Farra' said: by "al-batha'in" he meant the outer surfaces.

The historian said: it is in the language of the Copts, and the lining may be the outer surface and the outer surface the lining, because each of them may be a face. The Arabs say: "this is the back of the sky" and "this is the belly of the sky," for whoever sees it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the killers of 'Uthman: "Allah has killed them in the worst manner, and those of them who escaped fled under the bellies of the stars," meaning they fled by night, so he made the backs of the stars into bellies.

Al-Qutaybi said: this is from the strange interpretations. How can the lining be the outer surface, and the outer surface the lining?

The "batana" is that which is inside of a garment, and it was the custom of people to conceal it, while the "dhiharah" is that which shows, and it is the custom of people to display it. Could anyone say of the face of one praying, "this is its lining," or of what is on the earth's surface, "this is its outer surface"? No, by Allah, that is not permissible. Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.

﴿Two gardens﴾: two orchards of red ruby and green chrysolite, whose soil is camphor and ambergris, and whose clay is musk of the strongest fragrance. Each orchard is a journey of a hundred years, and in the middle of each orchard is a dwelling of light.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: one garden is for fear of one's Lord, and one garden is for abandoning one's desires. Muqatil said: they are the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: ﴿two gardens﴾ of gold are for the foremost, and two gardens of silver are for the followers.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Do you know what these two gardens are? They are two orchards among orchards; their foundation is firm, their branches are firm, and their trees are firm."

'Aqil informed me by licence, saying: al-Mu'afa informed us by recitation, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari informed us, saying:

Muhammad ibn Musa al-Jarshi related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Sa'id al-Hariri related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ I said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery, even if he steals, despite the nose of Abu al-Darda' [in the dust]."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Possessing branches [dhawata afnan].﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "afnan" means varieties, its singular being "fann," from the expression "iftanna fulan fi hadithihi" when he takes up its various kinds and forms. Al-Dahhak said: the varieties of fruits.

Mujahid said: branches, its singular being "fann" [or "fanan"]. 'Ikrimah said: the shade of the branches over the walls. Al-Hasan said: "possessing shades," which is like His saying: ﴿and extended shade﴾. Al-Dahhak also said: possessing branches and sections. He said: its branches are like trellised vines, touching one another. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: possessing excellence and abundance above all others. Ibn Kaysan said: possessing roots.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: with honour and increase over the people of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: they flow with pure water, one of them being Tasnim and the other Salsabil.

'Ata'iyyah said: one of them is of water unaltered [by time], and the other is of wine, delicious to those who drink. It was also said: they flow from a mountain of musk. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: ﴿In both of them are two flowing springs﴾ refers to whoever in this world had two eyes that flowed with weeping.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿In both of them are fruits of every kind, two of each.﴾ Two kinds.

Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world except that it is in Paradise, even the bitter colocynth, except that it is sweet.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on couches [mutaki'in]﴾, a state, ﴿whose linings are of brocade [istabraq]﴾, which is the thick and fine silk. It was also said: it is an Arabized word.

Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah said: these are the linings, so what do you think of the outer surfaces? It was said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The linings are of brocade, so what are the outer surfaces?" He said: This is among what Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾

He also said: ﴿Its linings are of brocade, and its outer surfaces are of solid light.﴾ Al-Farra' said: by "al-batha'in" he meant the outer surfaces.

The historian said: it is in the language of the Copts, and the lining may be the outer surface and the outer surface the lining, because each of them may be a face. The Arabs say: "this is the back of the sky" and "this is the belly of the sky," for whoever sees it. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said regarding the killers of 'Uthman: "Allah has killed them in the worst manner, and those of them who escaped fled under the bellies of the stars," meaning they fled by night, so he made the backs of the stars into bellies.

Al-Qutaybi said: this is from the strange interpretations. How can the lining be the outer surface, and the outer surface the lining?

The "batana" is that which is inside of a garment, and it was the custom of people to conceal it, while the "dhiharah" is that which shows, and it is the custom of people to display it. Could anyone say of the face of one praying, "this is its lining," or of what is on the earth's surface, "this is its outer surface"? No, by Allah, that is not permissible. Rather, Allah the Exalted and Most High wished to make us aware of His subtlety, by which He knows the excellence of these couches, and that what lies on the earth of them is brocade. If the lining is like that, then the outer surface is higher and more noble. Likewise is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The handkerchiefs of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh in Paradise are better than this garment." He mentioned the handkerchiefs specifically, rather than others, because they are the finest. What al-Qutaybi said confirms what we have related from Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah. And Allah knows best.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand﴾: its fruit is within reach, attainable by the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are those restraining their gaze, whom no man or jinn has touched before them.﴾ ﴿Restraining their gaze﴾: lowering their eyes, having confined their gaze to their husbands, so they do not look at others and do not desire others. Ibn Zayd said: she says to her husband, "By the might of my Lord, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you. Praise be to Allah who made you my husband and made me your wife."

﴿Whom no man has touched﴾: he did not have intercourse with them, nor did he deflower them. Its root is blood, and from it comes the term for a menstruating woman, "ta'ith," as if He said: he did not make them bleed through intercourse. ﴿Before them, nor jinn.﴾ Mujahid said: when a man has intercourse without mentioning the name of Allah, the jinn coils around his penis and has intercourse with him. That is His saying: ﴿whom no man or jinn has touched before them﴾, meaning, did not have intercourse with them.

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "If a woman dies in a state of virginity, she enters Paradise." [[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/125.]] And a poet said:

"They were handed to me, untouched before me,
and they are purer than ostrich eggs."
[[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/345; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/181, where "waqa'n" replaces "daf'n"; Lisan al-'Arab: 2/166, where "fahunna" replaces "wahunna."]]

Sahl said: whoever restrains his gaze in this world from pleasures will be compensated in the Hereafter with the restrainers of gaze. Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: I asked Damrah ibn Habib, "Do the jinn have reward?" He said: "Yes," and recited this verse, and said: "The human women are for men, and the jinn women are for jinn."

﴿As if they were ruby and coral.﴾ Qatadah said: the clarity of ruby within the whiteness of coral.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Sahl ibn 'Uthman al-'Maskari related to us, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, a woman of the people of Paradise, the whiteness of her shin is seen through seventy garments, until its marrow is seen. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿as if they were ruby and coral﴾. As for ruby, it is a stone: if you were to insert a thread into it and then drill it through, you would see it from its other side."

Sufyan related from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: "Indeed a woman of the houris will wear seventy garments, and the marrow of her shin will be seen from behind them, as red drink is seen in a white glass."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ The particle "hal" in Arabic speech has four uses:

The first: meaning "qad" (indeed), as in His saying: ﴿Has there come upon man [hal ata]﴾ and ﴿Has there come to you [hal ataka]﴾.

The second: meaning interrogation, as in His saying: ﴿Have you found [hal wajadtum] what your Lord promised to be true?﴾

The third: meaning command, as in His saying: ﴿So will you [hal antum] desist?﴾

The fourth: meaning "ma" of negation, as in His saying: ﴿Upon the messengers is only [hal 'ala al-rusul illa] the clear notification﴾, and ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good [hal jaza'u al-ihsani illa al-ihsan]?﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba, Ibn Hamdan, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl, and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Bahram related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Mukattib related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Husayn related to us, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ and said: "Do you know what your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed faith in monotheism anything but Paradise?"

Abu al-'Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi related to us verbatim, saying: My grandfather Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mubashshir related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-Ubulli related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Darimi related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ubadah, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ Allah the Exalted says: Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed knowledge of Me and monotheism anything but that I should settle him in My Garden and in the enclosure of My holiness, by My mercy?"

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Adi related to us, saying: Salih ibn Shu'ayb al-Khawwas related to us in Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Yamami related to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ He said: "Is the reward of one upon whom I have bestowed Islam anything but Paradise?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Is the reward of one who did good in this world, and said, 'There is no god but Allah,' anything but Paradise in the Hereafter? Is the reward of those who obeyed Me in this world anything but honour in the Hereafter?"

Al-Sadiq said: "Is the reward of one to whom You have done good in pre-eternity anything but the preservation of that goodness upon him forever?"

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah and al-Hasan said: it applies generally to the righteous and the wicked [for the wicked] [[Not present in the manuscript.]] in this world, and to the righteous in the Hereafter.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And besides these two﴾: that is, besides the first two gardens, ﴿there are two others.﴾ The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿besides these two﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "besides them" refers to rank. Ibn Zayd said: "besides them" refers to excellence. Ibn Zayd said: there are four: two gardens for the foremost, the near ones, ﴿therein are fruits of every kind, two of each﴾, and two gardens for the companions of the right and the followers, ﴿therein are fruit, palm trees, and pomegranates﴾. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Yahya said: He meant other gardens, because they are below the first two. Al-Kisa'i said: it means in front of them and before them, as the poet said:

"How many a desert lies beyond it, silencing the traveller,
and a hill that leads to hills."

That is, before the first wilderness. The evidence for this interpretation is the saying of al-Dahhak: the first two gardens are of gold and silver, and the other two are of ruby and emerald, and they are superior to the first two.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Dark green [mudhammatan]﴾: lush, black-green from their irrigation and the intensity of their greenness, because when greenness becomes intense it turns toward blackness. Dhu al-Rummah said:

"He clothed the hills with abundant soft Abyssinian [greenery],
its pairs and the high ridges of the uplands."

He made it "Abyssinian" because its greenness had grown intense. It was also said: "meeting each other."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿Therein are two gushing springs [nadda-khatan]﴾: full, bubbling, overflowing with water, never ceasing. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Muslim said: they spring forth and then flow. Ibn 'Abbas said: they gush with goodness and blessing upon the people of Paradise. Ibn Mas'ud [said]: they spray upon the friends of Allah with musk and camphor. Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "dakhkhatan" with water and varieties of fruit. Anas ibn Malik: they spray musk and ambergris in the homes of the people of Paradise, as rain spray pours down, and the root of "nadkh" is sprinkling, which is more than "nadkh."

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾

﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin.﴾ Al-Husayn and Qatadah said: They will not be asked about their sins, because Allah the Exalted knows them and has recorded them [against them] [[In the manuscript: "against it."]], and the angels have written them down against them. This is the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. Also from him: the angels will not question the criminals [[In the manuscript: "the criminals."]] because they recognize them by their marks, and the proof is what follows it. This view was also held by Mujahid. Also from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ and His words ﴿So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be questioned about his sin﴾ [[In the manuscript: "and He said."]]: He said, "He will not ask them, 'Did you do such and such?' because He knows that better than they do, but He will ask them, 'Why did you do such and such?'" 'Ikrimah also said: there are occasions in which they are questioned and occasions in which they are not. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: they will not be asked a question seeking information or relief, but they will be asked a question of reproach and rebuke. Abu al-'Aliyah said: no one other than the sinner is asked about the sin of the criminal.

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, which is the blackness of the face and the blueness of the eyes. ﴿They will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾: they will be dragged to the Fire and thrown into it. Then it will be said to them: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals, the polytheists, used to deny.﴾ ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot﴾ [[ān]]: its report has reached its end [i.e., it is intensely hot]. Qatadah said: it has been cooking since Allah created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of the verse is that they will move back and forth between the blazing Fire and the scalding water.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "Ān" is a valley from the valleys of Hell in which the pus of the people of the Fire is gathered. They will be driven to it while they are in shackles, and they will be immersed in that valley until their joints are loosened. Then they will come out of it, and Allah the Exalted will have created for them a new creation, and they will be cast back into the Fire. This is His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding water, boiling hot.﴾

﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you two deny?﴾ ﴿And for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens.﴾ That is, his standing before his Lord. It was also said: his standing before his Lord, as explained by His saying: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds.﴾ It was also said: the standing of his Lord over him, as explained by His saying: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who do not]?﴾ Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers Allah the Exalted and abandons it out of fear of Allah. Dhu al-Nun said: a sign of the fear of Allah is that His fear secures you from every other fear. Al-Suddi said: there are two things that are lost: the fear that unsettles and the longing that disturbs.
