And Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i, who said: al-Fadl ibn [Iyad] [[In the source: Ayyash.]] related to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿dark-eyed ones, confined in the tents﴾, he said: "The tent is a single pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, and it has four thousand gates of gold." [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/208.]]

al-Husayn informed me, he said: Abdullah ibn [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]] related to us, he said: [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]] Abu Shu'ayb Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Harrani, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Qurashi, related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Hilal al-Sukkari related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night of my Night Journey, I passed by a river whose banks were domes of coral, and I was called from it: 'Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah.'

I said: 'O Gabriel, who are these?' He said: 'These are maidens of the dark-eyed houris who asked their Lord for permission to greet you, and He permitted them.' They said: 'We are the immortal, so we do not die; we are the ones who live in bliss, so we do not despair [[In some narrations: do not speak.]] [forever; we are the content, so we never become angry] wives of noble men.'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿dark-eyed ones, confined in the tents﴾.

He said: "Restrained." [183] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/179.]]

﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ ﴿Untouched before them by any human or jinn﴾. The common readers recite it with a kasrah on the mim, which is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Abu Yahya al-Shami and Talhah ibn Musarrif recited both with a dammah. al-Kisa'i would kasrah one and damm the other, choosing between them. The reason for this is what Abu Muhammad Shaybah ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed me, Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus informed me, Ibn Shanabudh related to me, Ayyash ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari informed me, Abu Umar al-Duri related to us, from al-Kisa'i, who said: "When the first is raised, the second is kasrah; when the second is raised, the first is kasrah." He said: It is the recitation (qira'ah) of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i. He said: Abu Ishaq said: "I used to pray behind the companions of Ali ibn Abi Talib, and I would hear them reciting (yatmithhunna) with a kasrah on the mim." Al-Kisa'i used to recite one with a raised mim and the other with a kasrah on the mim, so as not to depart from these two reports, and both are dialects.

﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ ﴿Reclining on green cushions﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They are the gardens of Paradise, green and dyed. This is related from Ibn Abbas. Its singular is rafrafah, and rafarif is a plural of a plural.

al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The rafraf: the surplus of the sitting carpets." Another wording: "the surplus of the furnishings and sitting places." Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: "Green cushions placed above the furnishings."

al-Hasan and al-Qurazi: "Rugs." Ibn Uyaynah: "Cushions of silk" (al-zarabi). Ibn Kaysan: "The armrests," and this is one report.

Qatadah, from al-Hasan, and Abu Ubaydah: "The edge of a garment and its extra." And any wide garment among the Arabs is called rafraf.

Ibn Muqbil said:

"And we are the ones who alight, covering our sandals
with fallen pieces of fine silk and rafraf."

﴿and beautiful ʿabqariyy﴾: they are the zarabi and thick carpets, and it is a plural whose singular is ʿabqariyyah. It is reported from the Arabs that they call everything of carpeting ʿabqariyy.

Qatadah said: "ʿAbqari is the choice quality of zarabi." Mujahid said: "It is brocade."

Abu al-Aliyah: "Velvet carpets with fine pile." [[Lisan al-Arab: 1/447: tanafis with fine pile.]]

al-Hasan: "Thick carpets," meaning [thick] [[From Tafsir al-Tabari: 27/213; the manuscript reads "al-thikhakh".]]. al-Qutaybi: "Every embroidered garment among the Arabs is ʿabqariyy."

Abu Ubayd said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made."

Dhu al-Rummah said:

"Until the sandy hills seemed to be clothed
in embroidery of ʿAbqar, covered and fringed."
[[Al-Sihah: 2/542.]]

He said: It is said that ʿAbqar is a land inhabited by jinn.

The poet [Zuhayr] said:

"With a miser over it, a garden of ʿAbqar,
worthy of attaining one day, so that they may rise."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 4/535.]]

Qutrub said: "This is not attributed. Every excellent, virtuous, distinguished man [and others] is called ʿabqari among the Arabs." And from this is the hadith about Umar: "I have not seen an ʿabqari who excels in his excellence."

Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Mu'ammal related to us, reading it to him, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Saghani related to us [[Thus in the manuscript; some biographical works and others have al-Saghani.]], al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, and (ḥ).

And al-Husayn informed me, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Nasih related to us, Ahmad ibn Zuhayr ibn Harb related to us, Abu Ahmad al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Zawzani al-Artabani, who is the paternal cousin of Abdullah ibn Awn, related to us, from Asim al-Jahdari, from Abu Bakrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "Reclining on green cushions and ʿabqariyy beautiful; ﴿So which of the bounties of your Lord will you both deny? Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾" with the waw, as the Syrians read it, and so it is in their codices (mushaf).

The rest read: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾.
